title: Lee et al. 2019 (Motor Imagery) — EEG dataset and OpenBMI toolbox for three BCI paradigms: an investigation into BCI illiteracy
description: A comprehensive EEG dataset comprising 54 healthy subjects performing three major brain-computer interface (BCI) paradigms: motor imagery (MI), event-related potential (ERP), and steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) across two sessions. The dataset investigates BCI illiteracy rates and performance variations, revealing that while MI showed the highest illiteracy rate (53.7%), all participants could proficiently control at least one BCI paradigm type. Data includes 62-channel EEG recordings at 1000 Hz with auxiliary EMG channels, questionnaire responses, and resting-state recordings.
methods_description: 54 healthy subjects (age 24-35, 25 female, 29 male) participated in two sessions on different days. Each session included three BCI paradigms performed sequentially: ERP speller (36 symbols with face stimuli), binary motor imagery task (left/right hand grasping), and SSVEP (four target frequencies: 5.45, 6.67, 8.57, 12 Hz). EEG recorded at 1000 Hz using 62 Ag/AgCl electrodes with BrainAmp amplifier, nose-referenced and grounded to AFz, with impedance maintained below 10 kOhm. Each paradigm included offline training and online test phases of 100 trials each. Subjects seated 60 cm from a 21-inch LCD monitor. Demographic, physiological, and psychological data collected via questionnaire. Artifact data (eye blinking, eye movements, teeth clenching, arm flexing) and resting-state EEG also recorded.
